verdicts.title: Meta-Mathematics of Computational Complexity Theory
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We survey results on the formalization and independence of mathematical statements related to major open problems in computational complexity theory. Our primary focus is on recent findings concerning the (un)provability of complexity bounds within theories of bounded arithmetic. This includes the techniques employed and related open problems, such as the (non)existence of a feasible proof that P = NP.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract surveys formalization and independence of complexity bounds in bounded arithmetic, with no mention of Hodge decompositions, CNF resolution depth, or any algebraic-geometric invariant relevant to the conjecture.

verdicts.title: Notes on absolute Hodge classes
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We survey the theory of absolute Hodge classes. The notes include a full proof of Deligne's theorem on absolute Hodge classes on abelian varieties as well as a discussion of other topics, such as the field of definition of Hodge loci and the Kuga-Satake construction.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract describes a survey of absolute Hodge classes, Deligne's theorem on abelian varieties, and the Kuga-Satake construction — it has no connection to CNF formulas, resolution proof depth, or any complexity-theoretic claim.

verdicts.title: Geometric complexity theory and matrix powering
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Valiant's famous determinant versus permanent problem is the flagship problem in algebraic complexity theory. Mulmuley and Sohoni (Siam J Comput 2001, 2008) introduced geometric complexity theory, an approach to study this and related problems via algebraic geometry and representation theory. Their approach works by multiplying the permanent polynomial with a high power of a linear form (a process called padding) and then comparing the orbit closures of the determinant and the padded permanent.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns geometric complexity theory, matrix powering, and the permanent-versus-determinant problem, with no mention of Hodge decompositions, CNF formulas, or resolution proof depth. It shares only the broad 'algebraic geometry meets complexity' framing but does not interact with the specific conjectured bound.
